payload.original: Data-only representation of the Indiana State Board of Accounts five-report audit package for calendar years 2024 and 2025. Auditor findings, applicable criteria, unverified official responses, corrective plans, and remaining uncertainties are distinguished. Administrative findings are not treated as proof of criminal conduct or intent.
payload.title: Pike Township, Marion County, Indiana: Financial Audit Findings, 2024-2025

payload.original: The 2024 financial audit covered Pike Township's financial position and results of operations for 1 January through 31 December 2024. [PT-C001]
For 2024, SBOA issued an adverse opinion under U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and an unmodified opinion on the regulatory-basis financial statement. [PT-C002]

The 2024 supplemental report describes compliance procedures under Indiana Code 5-11-1 and reports instances SBOA considered noncompliance; the procedures were not designed to identify every noncompliance instance. [PT-C003]
SBOA found internal-control deficiencies that contributed to noncompliance in 2024. [PT-C005]

In a sample of 18 employees for 2024 payroll testing, one employee received two salary increases totaling $4,000 that were not authorized by the union contract, salary resolution, or another policy. [PT-C007]
SBOA's additional review identified multiple employees who received similar unauthorized increases in 2024 totaling $20,000. [PT-C008]
For 2024, SBOA requested a mileage log but one was not provided, and the auditors found no documentation showing that a log had been maintained during the audit period. [PT-C010]

The Trustee's 2024 response said officials had not understood that additional pay for expanded duties required salary-resolution approval, that the practice was discontinued until approval, and that future changes would be reviewed and included in the salary resolution. [PT-C012]

The Trustee's 2024 response said the vehicles were a shared pool and logs had not been consistently maintained; it said a trip log was placed in each vehicle and would be retained and monitored. [PT-C013]
The 2025 financial audit covered the Township's financial position and results of operations for 1 January through 31 December 2025. [PT-C016]
For 2025, SBOA again issued an adverse opinion under U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and an unmodified opinion on the regulatory-basis financial statement. [PT-C017]
SBOA found internal-control deficiencies that contributed to noncompliance in 2025. [PT-C019]

The 2025 Annual Financial Report grant schedule omitted part of Medical Assistance Program reimbursements from Indiana FSSA under Assistance Listing 93.778, understating the schedule by $1,022,949. [PT-C020]

In a sample of 16 employees for 2025 payroll testing, one employee received two salary increases totaling $4,000 that were not authorized by the union contract, salary resolution, or another policy. [PT-C022]
SBOA's additional review identified multiple employees who received similar unauthorized increases in 2025 totaling $20,000. [PT-C023]
For 2025, SBOA again requested a mileage log but one was not provided, and no documentation showed a log had been maintained during the audit period. [PT-C024]

Federal finding 2025-001 classified controls over preparation of the Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards as a material weakness and reported the same $1,022,949 understatement; proposed audit adjustments were accepted and made. [PT-C025]

The 2025 federal audit reported no federal award findings or questioned costs, issued an unmodified opinion on compliance for the major Medicaid Cluster program, and stated that Pike Township was not a low-risk auditee. [PT-C028]

The corrective action plan for finding 2025-001 says the Fire Department would forward Medicaid communications to accounting, the departments would reconcile EMS deposits, accounting would be copied on reimbursement notices, and receipts would be tracked for future annual reports. [PT-C029]
The 2025 corrective action plan lists immediate implementation and an anticipated completion date of 31 December 2026. [PT-C030]

payload.statement: The 2024 and 2025 findings show recurring weaknesses in compensation authorization, vehicle-use documentation, and related compliance controls.
The $1,022,949 matter was a federal-award reporting and review-control error corrected by audit adjustment, not an auditor finding that funds were missing or that the major program was noncompliant.

payload.mechanism: The reports establish management's statements and plans, not subsequent operating effectiveness.
payload.statement: The auditee responses and corrective action plan establish that the identified controls were implemented and operated effectively after the audit periods.

payload.mechanism: This is included as an expressly tested alternative so administrative findings are not silently criminalized.
payload.statement: The audit reports establish criminal conduct or intent.
